headline: US evacuates up to 12 aircraft from RAF Mildenhall after Iran threat
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the evacuation] The US military evacuated aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England on Monday Nov 9 after a threat from Iran (WSJ, citing people familiar with the matter). CNN flight-tracking analysis shows 10 US refueling aircraft relocated away from Mildenhall on Monday:…
sources: The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter; US official (FPCON Charlie); CNN flight-tracking analysis; Sky News flight-tracking sources
fault_line: Iran's threat reaches British soil: is pulling the tankers out smart force protection, or proof the US is running out of safe places to stage a strike on Iran?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the evacuation] The US military evacuated aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England on Monday Nov 9 after a threat from Iran (WSJ, citing people familiar with the matter). CNN flight-tracking analysis shows 10 US refueling aircraft relocated away from Mildenhall on Monday: 4 KC-135 Stratotankers to Spangdahlem Air Base (Germany), 1 to Ramstein (Germany), 4 to Moron Air Base (Spain), 1 to Glasgow Prestwick (Scotland). Sky News, citing flight-tracking sources, counts 12 aircraft leaving Mildenhall Monday: 9 tankers + 3 Osprey transporters. The National reports up to 12 refuelling aircraft flown out to US bases in Germany and Spain. [VERIFIED FACT -- the threat level] The US upgraded the security posture at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest defensive threat level, which applies when intelligence indicates a terrorist action is likely (WSJ citing a US official; confirmed to The War Zone by a US official). A security source told The National it was likely there was 'credible intelligence' Iran 'was preparing to engage in a drone attack targeting Mildenhall' with kamikaze drones. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the threat] The precise nature of the threat 'remains under discussion among US officials' (WSJ). Iran has said its retaliation for any US attack would expand beyond the Middle East. [CONTEXT] Second UK base in weeks: B-1 bombers were sent back to the US from RAF Fairford last month over a suspected Iran-backed plot to kill American pilots and target aircraft with drones. DNI Jay Clayton said in October that Iran was in 'advanced stages' of planning to target US personnel in the Middle East. Mildenhall hosts the 100th Air Refueling Wing -- the only permanent refueling wing in Europe (AP).
sections.what_verified: 5 distinct tiered publisher families: WSJ (T2) + Reuters (T1) + AP (T1) + The National (T2) + Sky News (T2). CNN (not in the source registry) reported with attribution only and does not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: (a) The Iran link is attributed, not confirmed by the Pentagon: a US Air Force spokesperson declined details and said aircraft 'rotate between installations and operating locations for a variety of reasons'; the White House referred comment to the Pentagon; the Pentagon did not immediately respond. (b) WSJ itself: the precise nature of the threat -- imminent or general -- 'remains under discussion among US officials'. (c) Counts differ by tracker: CNN 10 refueling aircraft vs Sky News 12 aircraft (9 tankers + 3 Ospreys) -- scope difference (refueling aircraft vs all aircraft), not a contradiction, but the exact number is tracker-dependent. (d) The National's 'kamikaze drones' detail rests on a single security source.
sections.why_matters: The war has reached Britain. The US just pulled its strike-enabling tankers out of a second UK base -- 10 to 12 aircraft gone in a day -- because Iran threatened to hit them with kamikaze drones. The base that refuels America's bombers is now a target itself.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (event Mon Nov 9; first publications 06:31-07:40 UTC = 10:31-11:40 ; not recorded) -- ELEVATION TRIGGER: US evacuates up to 12 aircraft from RAF Mildenhall after Iran threat; Mildenhall + Lakenheath raised to FPCON Charlie

totw_analysis: Our read: The war has reached Britain. The US just pulled its strike-enabling tankers out of a second UK base -- 10 to 12 aircraft gone in a day -- because Iran threatened to hit them with kamikaze drones. The base that refuels America's bombers is now a target itself. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Iran's threat reaches British soil: is pulling the tankers out smart force protection, or proof the US is running out of safe places to stage a strike on Iran?
